cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is wrapping up his letter to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2), and now he gets practical. First up: the collection for the saints. He tells them to handle it the same way he directed the churches of Galatia.

Here's the plan: every week, each of them sets aside a portion of his income and saves it up, so nothing has to be gathered when Paul comes. It's the cookie jar method, friend: a little goes in every week, until one day the lid won't CLOSE.

cards.question: Paul wants each of the Corinthians to set aside a portion of his income on the ___ day of every week.

cards.text: Once Paul gets to Corinth, that gift has a trip to make. And Paul will send letters along with it.

cards.question: Who does Paul say will carry the Corinthians' gift?
The people the Corinthians recommend will carry their gift to ___.
If it seems best for Paul to go too, the people carrying the gift can travel with him.

cards.text: Now the travel plans: Paul IS coming to Corinth, but he's going through Macedonia first. Hey, I had a stop of my own before I got HERE: years in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul might stay in Corinth a while, maybe even spend the winter. What does he hope the Corinthians will do for him after that?

answers.text: Help him on his journey wherever he goes
Keep the collection safe until spring
Give him a house to stay in for good

cards.text: Paul doesn't want to see them just in passing. This is NOT the friend who says he'll swing by, then honks from the driveway and pulls off.

cards.question: Paul hopes to spend some time with the Corinthians, but he puts one condition on it. What is it?

cards.text: But Corinth will have to wait a little: Paul is staying in Ephesus until Pentecost. A great door for effective work has opened to him there.

cards.question: In Ephesus, Paul says nobody is standing against his work.

cards.text: Next up: Timothy, a disciple Paul took along on his travels (Acts 16:1-3). If Timothy shows up in Corinth, Paul wants him to have nothing to fear while he's there.

cards.question: Why should the Corinthians make sure Timothy has nothing to fear with them?

answers.text: He is doing the work of the Lord like Paul
He is carrying the gift for the saints
He is Paul's own brother by birth

cards.question: Paul says no one should treat Timothy with ___.
Paul wants the Corinthians to keep Timothy with them for good.

cards.text: Then there's Apollos, a teacher who had already worked in Corinth (Acts 18:27-19:1; 1 Corinthians 3:6). Paul calls Apollos our brother, and Paul STRONGLY urged Apollos to go to Corinth with the brothers.

cards.question: Paul strongly urged Apollos to go to Corinth. Where does Apollos land on it?

answers.text: Not now but he'll go when he has the chance
Yes and he'll leave with the brothers right away
No and he never plans to go back there

cards.text: Then Paul goes rapid-fire: "Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong." That's not a letter anymore, friend, that's a coach at HALFTIME.
And then one more line that covers everything they do: "Do everything in love."
Then Paul brings up Stephanas and his household, the family Paul baptized himself (1 Corinthians 1:16). He reminds the Corinthians of something they already know about them.

cards.question: Stephanas and his household were the first ___ in Achaia.
Stephanas's household has devoted itself to serving the saints. How does Paul urge the brothers to treat people like that?

answers.text: Submit to them and every fellow worker
Pay them wages from the collection
Send them out to start new churches

cards.text: Turns out Stephanas has arrived where Paul is, along with Fortunatus and Achaicus. Paul is glad, because they supplied what was lacking from the Corinthians.

cards.question: Paul says Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus ___ his spirit, and the Corinthians' spirit as well.
Paul tells the Corinthians to show their appreciation to men like these.

cards.text: Then the greetings pile in: the churches in the province of Asia, Aquila and Prisca, Paul's fellow workers in Christ Jesus (Romans 16:3), the church that meets at their house, and all the brothers with Paul. It's like a birthday card that got passed around the WHOLE office.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to greet one another with a holy kiss.

cards.text: Then Paul writes this greeting in his own hand, and signs it: Paul.
Then comes a hard line: "If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse." And right after it: "Come, O Lord!"

cards.question: After that hard line, what does Paul wish for the Corinthians as he signs off?

answers.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus and Paul's own love
Safe travels for the gift to Jerusalem
Patience as they wait for Timothy
